corrected_text: tPA (alteplase) for ischemic stroke: Door-to-needle goal <60 minutes (ideally <30 min). Window: <3 hours per FDA labeling; AHA/ASA guidelines support use up to 4.5 hours from symptom onset with relative exclusion criteria (age >80, on anticoagulation, NIHSS >25, combined prior stroke+DM2). Last known well = symptom onset time. Non-contrast CT head required to rule out hemorrhage before tPA. Alteplase dose: 0.9 mg/kg (max 90 mg), 10% as bolus over 1 min, remainder over 60 min. Note: Tenecteplase (TNK) 0.25 mg/kg IV bolus (max 25 mg) is an alternative increasingly preferred. Concurrent antiplatelet agents generally avoided first 24 hrs.

corrected_text: After tPA: no anticoagulation or antiplatelet for 24 hours. Neuro checks every 15 min x 2 hours, then q30 min x 6 hours, then hourly x 16 hours. ICU admission typical. Repeat CT 24 hours after tPA to rule out hemorrhagic transformation (10-15% of tPA cases; usually asymptomatic). Monitor for symptomatic ICH (volume hemorrhage with clinical deterioration). Hypertension management post-tPA: maintain SBP <180 mmHg AND DBP <105 mmHg for first 24 hours; treat promptly with labetalol IV or nicardipine infusion if above threshold.

Blood pressure: for SBP 150-220, target SBP <140 mmHg (AHA 2022 guidelines); avoid excessive lowering (ischemia risk; do not lower if SBP <150). Avoid hypoxia, hypercarbia, fever (treat aggressively), hyperglycemia (target 140-180). DVT prophylaxis delayed while ICH active. Surgical consultation if mass effect, lobar hemorrhage with herniation risk, or posterior fossa hemorrhage. Medications for BP control: labetalol or nicardipine IV infusion. Mannitol or hypertonic saline for elevated ICP/herniation. Repeat CT head after 6h to assess for hematoma expansion.
